name: M-Lab Starlink Connectivity Source Nodes
description: M-Lab NDT statistics pipeline -> SDS $CNP constellation-network-performance records. Two pure flow nodes: `request` turns a cron timer tick into ONE whole-file hostcap/http-request GET of https://statistics.measurementlab.net/v0/asn/<ASN>/<YEAR>/histogram_daily_stats.json (anonymous HTTPS, no BigQuery, no auth) plus the parser attribution job; `parse` joins that job with the http response, collapses the eight per-date log-bucket rows into one aggregate per UTC day and emits a size-prefixed $CNP record stream for hostcap/storage-ingest. Starlink IS the client-ASN key: the upstream query groups by client.Network.ASNumber and AS14593 is SPACEX-STARLINK, so no constellation is ever inferred from a throughput number. A quantity exists only as a CNPMetric with UNITS and PROVENANCE, and CNPMetric has no scalar VALUE: throughput publishes six CNPStatistic entries (MINIMUM, PERCENTILE 25, MEDIAN, MEAN, PERCENTILE 75, MAXIMUM) in Mbps verbatim and minimum-RTT publishes exactly one MEDIAN in ms. REGION is omitted entirely because the per-ASN export carries no geographic key. M-Lab test data is CC0, so every metric carries LICENSE CC0-1.0, M-Lab's own citation in ATTRIBUTION and NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY false. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O — http and storage are the generic hostcap connector nodes. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted on the parse node: the method emits a single notice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

sequentialJustification.detail: Both methods are pure single-pass transforms over one fetched JSON table: `request` formats a fetch descriptor from node CONFIG, and `parse` walks the M-Lab per-ASN statistics rows once, collapsing the eight bucket rows of each date into a single $CNP record appended to one output stream. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool, no fan-out and nothing for a second thread to do; the whole cost is one linear scan of a ~0.5 MB body. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles on the single-thread STANDALONE_WASM lane rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Builds the M-Lab per-ASN statistics fetch request + parse job from a timer tick. ONE whole-file request per cycle (the statistics pipeline publishes a static per-ASN-per-year artifact, not a paged API) with an identifying User-Agent and conditional-request validators from node CONFIG. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.

wildcardJustification.detail: Cron timer tick frame produced by the flow runtime and consumed inside this flow only; it carries no payload at all, so there is no SDS record to name.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON http request for the M-Lab per-ASN statistics file.

wildcardJustification.detail: hostcap/http-request request descriptor ({method,url,headers,timeoutMs}) produced and consumed inside this flow; its shape is defined by the host http.request op, not by SDS.
Fetch-job attribution ({source_url,source_name,provider_id,archive_*}) produced and consumed inside this flow; it is ingest bookkeeping, never persisted as a record.

methods.description: Collapses the eight per-date log-bucket rows of the M-Lab per-ASN export into one $CNP aggregate per UTC day (WINDOW_START inclusive, WINDOW_STOP exclusive, AGGREGATION_PERIOD DAY) and emits a size-prefixed $CNP record stream plus the storage.ingest_with_source meta and the raw payload for archiving. Throughput stays in Mbps and RTT in ms — units are never silently converted — and the histogram columns and geometric means are recorded as unencoded in the batch provenance rather than forced into a CNPStatistic that would mean something else. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted, never treated as a failed fetch: the host presents the ETag / Last-Modified it recorded from the previous 2xx for this URL, so an unchanged export answers 304 with no body. The method then emits a single notice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

wildcardJustification.detail: Fetch-job attribution ({source_url,source_name,provider_id,archive_*}) emitted by this module's own request node inside the same flow; ingest bookkeeping, never persisted.

wildcardJustification.detail: storage.ingest_with_source meta (schema, provider/source/url/batch attribution, reconcile mode, archive naming, licence-bearing provenance) consumed by hostcap/storage-ingest inside this flow.

wildcardJustification.detail: The verbatim M-Lab per-ASN histogram_daily_stats.json as fetched from statistics.measurementlab.net, archived byte-for-byte for provenance. It is an external wire format with no SDS identity.

HTTP 304 notice {status:304,unchanged:true,source_name,source_url,dataset_id} produced when the origin confirms the previously fetched document is current; delivered to the flow's egress sink, never persisted as a record.

outputPorts.description: Emitted ONLY when the fetch answered HTTP 304 Not Modified (the host sent the recorded ETag / Last-Modified validators): one notice frame and no meta/records/raw frames, so the ingest node never becomes ready and nothing is stored or announced.
